clue.text: Angry following fine after tasting evening at the deli?

parts.note: a cheese do is an informal party where cheeses are sampled
F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references
F stands for fine on pencil grades

explanation.surface: Someone gets cross after a fine is imposed following a deli's tasting night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the two F's behind the party; a 'do' is British slang for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheesed off is British slang for being irritated, fed up or annoyed.

clue.text: A third of revenue sequestered in place of business space

indicators.note: sequestered means locked away inside something

parts.note: the City is London's financial district
taken as written

indicators.note: a third here means the third letter of the following word

parts.note: third letter of the word

explanation.surface: Tax revenue hidden away in a business premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A third of' reads as one-third of the money, but it means the third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavity is a hollow, an empty space within a solid body.

clue.text: Ring partly interrupting time signal we hear

indicators.note: something interrupting breaks into the middle of another

parts.note: an eon is a vast age
an arc is part of a circle

explanation.surface: A phone ring cuts across the radio's time signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An earcon is a brief distinctive sound used by computers, the audio counterpart of an icon.

clue.text: "What is useful for alpine climber?" My answer's ski pants in case of splits

indicators.note: splits means breaks apart, so the condition word sits inside the jumble
pants is British slang for rubbish, so the words before it are messed up

parts.note: taken as written
'in case of rain' amounts to 'if it rains'

explanation.surface: A climber asks what to carry and is told ski trousers, in case they tear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like trousers, but it is the anagram signal, and 'splits' tells you where IF goes.
explanation.definitionFit: This multi-tool penknife from Switzerland has blades and gadgets handy for a mountaineer.

clue.text: Outlaw recycling poet's works on a trailer

indicators.note: recycling sends the front letter round to the back of the word

parts.note: odes are lyric poems
as in a price per item, so much on each
a trailer advertises a film

explanation.surface: A criminal reuses a poet's output for a film preview.
explanation.walkthrough: Elgar gives no signal for the insertion: the two short pieces simply slip in before the letter that has moved to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless bandit or criminal of the Wild West.

clue.text: A little of what Genevan makes from farm that's out of bounds

definitions.text: A little of what Genevan makes

indicators.note: out of its bounds means stripped of its boundary letters at both ends

parts.note: as in made of or from
a ranch is a large farm

explanation.surface: A Swiss citizen earns money from farmland that is off limits.
explanation.walkthrough: Geneva is in Switzerland, whose currency unit this is.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss franc is the currency a Geneva resident is paid in, one unit of their earnings.

clue.text: "Ruler" — not a word I understand

parts.note: a call for silence, asking that not a word be spoken
an exclamation of sudden comprehension

explanation.surface: Someone admits to not understanding a single word of the term ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A shah was the hereditary monarch of Iran, so a sovereign head of state.

clue.text: Embrace noble quality, uplifting Calvinist

parts.note: to hold in your arms
U means upper-class

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting a word up turns it backwards

parts.note: tone is a characteristic quality, as of sound

explanation.surface: A Calvinist's embrace has an elevating, noble character.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Huguenots were French Protestants who followed the teachings of John Calvin.

clue.text: Punch opportunist in the sun?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a wild swinging blow
second meaning: one who makes hay while the sun shines

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'make hay while the sun shines' means to seize an opportunity.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a powerful roundhouse blow and a farm worker cutting and drying grass.

clue.text: I trap these people in wee game

indicators.note: in puts the earlier words inside the word for wee

parts.note: informal for urinate
taken as written
a gin is a snare for catching animals
pronoun for those referred to

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to trapping people in a tiny game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wee' looks like Scottish for small but here it means to urinate.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig in the middle is a children's ball game where one player tries to intercept throws between two others.

clue.text: Musician burned in the nude?

indicators.note: a nude figure is stripped of its outer covering, so the outside letters come off

parts.note: burned food was cooked too long

explanation.surface: A query about someone getting sunburnt while sunbathing naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi was the Italian opera composer of Aida and La Traviata.

clue.text: With economy, standard parts for each individual

indicators.note: to part something is to split it open, so the second word is split around the first

parts.note: one at a time, each on its own
par is the expected standard, as in golf

explanation.surface: An economy measure in which a standard ration is divided out to each person.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something sparingly means using as little as possible, frugally and thriftily.

clue.text: DeMille's last will and testament all about satirical film

indicators.note: turning all of the gathered pieces about means reading them backwards
the last of a name means just its final letter is kept

parts.note: end letter of the director's surname
'he will go' can be put as 'he is to go'
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Cecil B DeMille's final will is said to concern a satirical movie.
explanation.walkthrough: The three pieces, E, IS TO and OT, are strung together and then the whole string is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tootsie is the 1982 Dustin Hoffman comedy satirising sexism in the television industry.

clue.text: Fancy that woman? Not in a hundred years

indicators.note: in places the pronoun between the century and the years

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for one hundred
not her but the masculine object pronoun
an era is a long span of years

explanation.surface: Someone is asked whether they fancy a woman and replies: not in a hundred years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like the verb for attraction, but it is a noun: a wild imagining.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a figment of the imagination, an illusory dream or flight of fantasy.

clue.text: Spooner said feeling strain ruined Peaty's style

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of neighbouring words

parts.note: under pressure, pronounced 'strest'
financially ruined, with no money left
swapping the opening sounds of the two words

explanation.surface: A swimmer's technique is wrecked by the stress he feels.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam Peaty is a British Olympic champion swimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Peaty won his Olympic golds in this frog-kick swimming stroke, his specialist event.

clue.text: Pass over new setting, being snubbed in New Orleans style

indicators.note: in puts the earlier pieces inside the jazz style

parts.note: trad is traditional jazz of the New Orleans kind

indicators.note: snubbed suggests a cut-short nose, so the word loses its tip

parts.note: N abbreviates new
the setting of a story

explanation.surface: A jazz performer ignores a new arrangement that has been coldly rejected.
explanation.definitionFit: To transcend is to go beyond or rise above limits, crossing over them.

clue.text: Counters a bent Uber maybe employs

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: bent round, the word doubles back on itself

parts.note: an Uber is an example of a taxi
puts to use

explanation.surface: A dishonest ride-share company is said to use counter-measures.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a bead frame used for counting, so abacuses are counting devices.

clue.text: State occasion illicitly screens to the north

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means reading upwards
something that screens conceals a thing behind it

parts.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A government event is secretly shown in northern cinemas.
explanation.definitionFit: Illinois is a Midwestern American state whose largest city is Chicago.

clue.text: Boy's name I'll primarily take before mixing?

definitions.text: Boy's name I'll primarily take before mixing?

indicators.note: mixing stirs the letters together into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: primarily means first, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: opening letter of the verb

explanation.surface: Someone asks what name a lonely boy should give before socialising at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue describes a friendless lad who has to supply a name before he can mingle.
explanation.definitionFit: Billy No-Mates is British slang for a person with no friends, always alone.

clue.text: Extra fat cat wants the lot

parts.note: a nob is a wealthy, posh person
everything

explanation.surface: A greedy rich person wants even more, everything going.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a no-ball is an illegal delivery that gives the batting side an extra run.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-ball counts among cricket's extras, runs not scored off the bat.

clue.text: Refuse to sanction duck fat

indicators.note: to refuse something is to turn it away, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
to permit
a duck is a cricket score of nought, the shape of O; this is the removed letter

explanation.surface: Someone declines to approve of cooking with duck fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallow is rendered animal fat, used historically for candles and soap.

clue.text: Red letter day and it's left out

indicators.note: out suggests the remaining letters are knocked out of order
something left behind is dropped, so the day goes missing

parts.note: a letter of the Greek alphabet
taken as written
D abbreviates day; it is the letter removed

explanation.surface: A red-letter day, a special occasion, has been missed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red letter day' reads as one phrase, but 'Red' is the definition and 'letter' alone gives the Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a Tuscan wine, usually red, so an example of a red.

clue.text: Your setter's past the stage of perfection

parts.note: the setter speaking of themself: I am
in the past

explanation.surface: The compiler boasts of being beyond the point of perfection.
explanation.definitionFit: An imago is the final adult form of an insect, its fully developed phase after metamorphosis.

clue.text: Philosopher visiting Australia in spring

indicators.note: in places the visiting phrase inside the word for a spring

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
Oz is informal for Australia, so being there is being in Oz

explanation.surface: A thinker spends a springtime holiday in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season but is a source of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Baruch Spinoza was the seventeenth-century Dutch rationalist thinker who wrote the Ethics.

clue.text: Crystal set's reduced sealing at once meeting with criticism

indicators.note: sealing means shutting something inside, so the shortened word wraps the rest
reduced means cut short, so the word loses its end

parts.note: taken as written
immediately
flak is hostile criticism

explanation.surface: An old crystal radio set is cut back and immediately draws complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crystal set' reads as an early radio, but 'Crystal' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Each flake of snow is an ice crystal with six-fold symmetry.

clue.text: Slowly, say, coming from the right? Coming from the right

indicators.note: coming from the right means read leftwards, from the end back to the start

parts.note: anything moving away from the right heads leftward, shortened here

explanation.surface: The same phrase is repeated, once as a question and once as its answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slowly, say' is an instruction: speak slowly. The repeated phrase does two jobs, first giving a direction and then telling you to read it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To drawl is to speak in a slow, lazy manner with lengthened vowels.

clue.text: Help one's leader only moderately

parts.note: the distress call

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of the word one

explanation.surface: Someone's boss helps only a little.
explanation.definitionFit: So-so means mediocre, middling, neither good nor bad.

clue.text: Jolly intimate, St Robin?

parts.note: as in 'jolly good', pleasant
a close companion or comrade

explanation.surface: A cheerful close friend, perhaps called Robin.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin Goodfellow is another name for Puck in A Midsummer Night's Dream; the question mark admits he is hardly a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: The mischievous sprite Robin Goodfellow carries this surname, so it completes the name.
